Essential knowledge

Organ is in homeostasis with stress placed on it

Increase, decrease, or change in stress on an organ can result in cellular adaptations

Cellular adaptations

Hypertrophy

Hyperplasia

Atrophy

Metaplasia

Physiologic

Pathologic

Hypertrophy

Hypertrophy is increase in cell size

Caused by increase in stress

It can be physiologic or pathologic

Pathologic hypertrophy if not relieved can progress to cell injury and cell death

Mechanism of hypertrophy

Cardiac hypertrophy: Occur due to stretch

Release of mediators that stimulate cell growth (growth factors and hormones) => turn on signal transduction => induce expression of genes => genes encode number of cellular proteins => one result is synthesis of myofilaments which increases force generated with each contraction => cell meets increased work demands

Other mechanism is maybe the switch of contractile proteins from adult to fetal or neonatal forms (e.g. switch of α myosin heavy chain to β myosin heavy chain) => this will produce slower and stronger contractions

Hyperplasia

Hyperplasia is increase in the number of cells in an organ

It can be physiologic or pathologic

Pathologic hyperplasia vs cancer: responsive vs unresponsive to regulatory signals

Atrophy

Atrophy is reduced organ size caused by reduction in size and number of cells

Atrophy can be physiologic or pathologic

Mechanism of atrophy

Combination of decreased protein synthesis and increased protein degradation

Decrease protein synthesis is due to reduced metabolic activity

Protein degradation occur mainly by the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway

Atrophy also accompanied by increased autophagy

Metaplasia

Metaplasia is a change in which one adult cell type is replaced by another adult cell type

Caused by change in stress

Mechanism of metaplasia

Reprogramming of stem cells

Examples of metaplasia

Respiratory epithelium metaplasia from ciliated columnar to stratified squamous epithelium due to prolonged cigarette smoking

Lower esophagus stratified squamous metaplasia to intestinal type columnar epithelium due to chronic gastric reflux

  • Keratomalacia: squamous epithelium of conjunctiva undergoes metaplasia to stratified keratinizing squamous epithelium
  • Myositis ossificans

Malignant transformation in metaplasia

If the causes that led to metaplasia are persistent then it may predispose to malignant transformation of the epithelium
